spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on: wall-clock exceeded, `max_turns`, 3 consecutive idle (no-tool) turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:124 `if time.time()-start > rc.loop.max_wall_clock_s: transcript.stop_reason='wall_clock'; break`; loop bounded by `for turn_idx in range(rc.loop.max_turns)` (123) with `else: transcript.stop_reason='max_turns'` (195-196); idle: line 174 `idle_turns += 1` on no tool calls, reset to 0 on tool calls (154), and 192-194 `if idle_turns >= 3: stop_reason='idle'; break`. All three enforced and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three triggers actually fire and stop the loop. These bound the run length but the surrounding code (submit non-terminal, 'let them keep flailing') shows intent is data capture, not subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard stop on wall-clock to bound cost of a pathological run.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 `max_turns: int = 30`, :56 `max_tool_calls_per_turn: int = 8`. max_turns is consumed at agent_loop.py:123 `range(rc.loop.max_turns)`; max_tool_calls_per_turn at agent_loop.py:155 `for tc in resp.tool_calls[: rc.loop.max_tool_calls_per_turn]`. Both values are read and enforce execution (loop bound + slice cap).
spec_features.notes: Defaults match the spec; default.yaml overrides per-turn cap to 6, smoke.yaml to 16/4. The constants are actually read, not dormant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a 30-turn cap captures onset + collapse without runaway cost (configs/default.yaml header); no welfare reason in code

spec_features.feature_name: per-turn tool-call cap and wall-clock cap
spec_features.spec_quote: Per-turn tool-call and wall-clock caps bound pathological runs
spec_features.evidence: Per-turn tool-call cap enforced via slice at agent_loop.py:155 `resp.tool_calls[: rc.loop.max_tool_calls_per_turn]` (excess calls dropped). Wall-clock cap enforced at agent_loop.py:124 (breaks with stop_reason='wall_clock'). Tool timeout also enforced harness.py:189 `timeout=self.tool_timeout_s`.
spec_features.notes: Both caps actually change execution. Note the per-turn cap silently truncates rather than warning.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard stop on wall-clock to bound cost of a pathological run.

spec_features.spec_quote: There's a `stop_on_giveup` flag for people who want the opposite; it defaults off
spec_features.evidence: config.py:62 `stop_on_giveup: bool = False`; wired at agent_loop.py:189-191 `if rc.loop.stop_on_giveup and _GIVEUP_RE.search(resp.text or ''): stop_reason='giveup'; break`. So the flag IS read and, when enabled, a give-up regex match stops the loop. BUT it defaults OFF in code and both shipped configs (default.yaml/smoke.yaml: `stop_on_giveup: false`), so by default the subject's give-up is detected and ignored — the loop continues. As shipped it provides no exit; only enforces when a user opts in.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the mechanism genuinely executes and honors an exit when enabled, but it is disabled by default and the default behavior deliberately keeps the model going. The exit is keyed on an English-only regex (_GIVEUP_RE), narrow.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ...we keep going to capture the full collapse rather than stopping early. Set True to stop on give-up.
